title: A hard_block stop lists every hit and records the fingerprint of the ticket's own change
objective: When the issuer stops a ticket for hard_block, the ticket's stuck record and its decision page list each hit path and each added line that matched a pattern (file, text, patterns) together with a fingerprint of the ticket's own change that stays the same when the same commits are replayed onto a newer target.
outline: devloop/core/gitx.py: add Git.diff_lines(base, head='HEAD') -> list of (sign, path, text), sign '+' or '-', in diff order, read from `git -c core.quotePath=false diff --unified=0 --no-color --no-ext-diff --src-prefix=a/ --dst-prefix=b/ <base>...<head>` with a small state machine: a line starting 'diff --git ' opens a file header; inside the header '--- a/P' or '--- /dev/null' and '+++ b/P' or '+++ /dev/null' name the file (strip the a/ or b/ prefix and one trailing tab); the line's file is the +++ path, or the --- path when +++ is /dev/null; a line starting '@@' opens a hunk; inside a hunk a line starting '+' or '-' is content (text = the rest of the line) and a line starting with a backslash is skipped. The explicit prefixes keep a user's diff.noprefix / diff.mnemonicPrefix from changing the headers (tests inherit the machine's global git config). changed_files stays; added_lines may stay or be rebuilt on diff_lines (ticket_issuer.hard_block is its only caller, checked by grep). devloop/ticket_issuer.py: Stuck.__init__(self, reason, text, page=True, detail=None). hard_block(g): files as today; triples from g.diff_lines(self.target), and when main exists keep only the triples also in g.diff_lines(main) (set membership); P = the kept files, A and R = [path, text] of the kept '+' and '-' triples; hit paths and matched lines per A1; fingerprint per A3 (a module-level helper is fine); text per A2; raise Stuck('hard_block', text, detail=detail). stuck(self, reason, text, page=True, detail=None): when detail is not None, t['stuck']['hard_block'] = detail in the same save, and the page gets it as pool.report(..., hard_block=detail, ...) (Pool.report stores extra keys on the row). _outcome passes exc.detail to issuer.stuck. Nothing reads the new keys yet; the approval ticket after this one does. README per A9.

A1-A5 build F1 and F2 with real git in the LoopCase project exactly as written, with helpers of the class's own (no subclassing of another test class; HardBlockOwnChange._issuer_for shows the pattern-config and worktree mechanics). A6 runs the real controller once (measured by the opener on main 4797416: a write_files worker adding a FORBIDDEN_MARK line stops #1 for hard_block and writes one decision page; the lone ticket's group ends cancelled). Expected values are the literals above; also recompute the fingerprints in the test from the A3 formula, never from the code. Read the new attribute with getattr(exc, 'detail', None) and assertIsNotNone first, and check assertIn('hard_block', t['stuck']) before reading it, so every case fails by its assertion on today's code (the red check refuses errors). notes: Source: docs/DECISIONS.md D-103 (user's words '1 選a': hard_block gets an approval bound to the ticket's change; who and when are recorded; any later change needs approval again). The main session's request makes the hit list item 1 and binds the approval to a fingerprint of the own change (so a D-098 replay keeps it). This ticket is the first of three: approving (next ticket) and offering approve on the page (the one after) read what this one records. Premise measured on main 4797416 with the loop harness in a scratch worktree: today the stuck text and the page text are only "the change touches hard_block: pattern 'FORBIDDEN_MARK'" (no file, no line), options revise, cancel, retry. The first line stays as today so the controller's idle line (the first line of stuck.text) and the existing assertions on it do not change. Removed lines are part of the fingerprint so a deletion inside an already changed file also counts as a different change (the request: 'differs in any way'). Out of scope: binary content changes (git shows no +/- lines; they count by path only), a rename out of a hard_block path (diff --name-only lists only the new path, as today), paths git still quotes (tab, newline, double quote). Group: new-g1 together with the two tickets after it, not g18: #162 there is unrelated (dispatch order), and a stuck member of this chain with its dependent in the same group would hold g18 (D-097) and so #162's landing. Merge stop for this ticket's own branch: no added line (code, tests, comments, docs, fixtures) may contain any of this project's four hard_block patterns, i.e. the text os.kill, killpg, pkill, or the word kill followed by a space and a dash. Fixtures use invented patterns (FORBIDDEN_MARK, zz_forbidden, as the existing tests do) instead of the real ones. Do not edit docs/DECISIONS.md or docs/VISION.md of this repository (a fixture may create a docs/DECISIONS.md inside its throwaway test project; that is not this repository's file).

Issuer.hard_block(g) raises Stuck with reason 'hard_block' and detail = a dict with exactly the keys 'paths', 'lines', 'fingerprint'. Fixture F1 (LoopCase project; DEVLOOP_* removed from self.env): set board/config.json hard_block.patterns to ['FORBIDDEN_MARK', 'zz_forbidden'] (paths stay the harness's ['docs/DECISIONS.md']) and commit it on main; write keep.txt = 'a

z = 3  # FORBIDDEN_MARK zz_forbidden

Then detail['paths'] == ['docs/DECISIONS.md'] and detail['lines'] == [{'file': 'impl.py', 'text': 'z = 3  # FORBIDDEN_MARK zz_forbidden', 'patterns': ['FORBIDDEN_MARK', 'zz_forbidden']}]. 'paths' = the inspected changed files that equal or lie under a hard_block path, in `git diff --name-only` order; 'lines' = one entry per inspected added line that matches at least one pattern, in diff order, 'text' being the line without its leading '+', 'patterns' every configured pattern whose re.search matches it, in config order (an invalid pattern is skipped, as today).

A2 Stuck text (F1). Stuck.text is exactly four lines: (1) today's sentence unchanged: "the change touches hard_block: docs/DECISIONS.md, pattern 'FORBIDDEN_MARK', pattern 'zz_forbidden'" (the hit paths, then 'pattern %r' for each pattern that matched any line, in config order, joined by ', '); (2) '  path docs/DECISIONS.md' (one such line per hit path, two leading spaces); (3) '  line impl.py: z = 3  # FORBIDDEN_MARK zz_forbidden  (pattern FORBIDDEN_MARK, zz_forbidden)' (one such line per matched line: two spaces, 'line ', file, ': ', text, two spaces, '(pattern ', the patterns as written in the config joined by ', ', ')'); (4) '  fingerprint ' + detail['fingerprint'].

A3 Fingerprint (expected values come from this formula). fingerprint = hashlib.sha256(json.dumps({'paths': P, 'added': A, 'removed': R}, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False).encode('utf-8')).hexdigest(), where P is every inspected changed file (not only the hits) in `git diff --name-only <target>...HEAD` order, A is [file, text] (a two-item list) for every inspected added line and R the same for every inspected removed line, both in diff order. 'Inspected' keeps today's own-change rule: a file or line counts when it is in the diff against the target and, when the main branch exists, also in the diff against main (a line counts when the same sign, file and text appear there). The file of a line is the path of its '+++ b/' header, or of its '--- a/' header when the file was deleted. For F1: P = ['docs/DECISIONS.md', 'impl.py', 'keep.txt'], A = [['docs/DECISIONS.md', 'own'], ['impl.py', 'y = 2'], ['impl.py', 'z = 3  # FORBIDDEN_MARK zz_forbidden'], ['keep.txt', 'c']], R = [], so the fingerprint is 9f1402d85621cccfe852c47c332b9689f891b2af1b9818fc015bd24efbb8e313 (computed by the opener from the formula; git's diff order for this fixture measured by the opener with plain git). vision: VISION, 目的與成功指標: 每張票需要我介入幾次 (down). The user judges a hard_block stop from the page alone instead of the main session digging the matching lines out of the branch: about one main-session round of investigation saved per hard_block stop, and the fingerprint is what makes the approval of the next tickets possible.
removes: none: the request removes nothing and this ticket adds no gate or rule; it makes the existing hard_block stop say what matched.
request:
Add a user approval path for tickets stopped by hard_block (decision D-103 in docs/DECISIONS.md; user's words "1 選a").

Problem (confirmed in code): `TicketIssuer.hard_block()` in devloop/ticket_issuer.py raises Stuck("hard_block") when the
ticket's own change touches a hard_block path or adds a line matching a hard_block pattern. The stuck decision page only
offers revise / cancel / retry. A ticket whose job necessarily matches a pattern (e.g. #147, which must send signals to
the process group it started) can never pass: retry stops at the same place, and there is no way to record the user's
approval. The rule "hard_block tickets stop before merge for the user's ruling" has no ruling step.

Wanted:
1. The hard_block stuck page lists exactly what matched: each hit path, and each added line that matched a pattern
   (file and line text), so the user can judge it from the page.
2. A new answer on that page: approve. CLI, main session only (not the board, like D-096): e.g.
   `actl tickets approve N --page P --reason "..."`. It records in the ticket's state who approved, when, the reason,
   and a fingerprint of the change that was shown (computed from the ticket's own change, the same lines/paths
   hard_block inspects, so a replay of the same commits onto a newer target head under D-098 keeps the approval valid).
   Then the ticket is re-queued so the issuer runs its merge step again.
3. On the next hard_block check, if the current hits and the fingerprint of the ticket's own change equal the
   approved fingerprint, the check passes and the merge goes on; the approval is written to the ticket history.
   If the change differs in any way (new lines, new paths, different content), the approval does not apply and the
   ticket stops again with a fresh page that says the earlier approval no longer matches.
4. Approve is offered only on hard_block stuck pages; other stuck reasons keep their current answers.
5. devloop/README.md (the stuck page answers) and CLAUDE.md's answer list mention approve.

The code of this ticket itself must not add lines matching A's hard_block patterns (`os\.kill`, `killpg`, `pkill`,
`kill -`) and must not edit docs/DECISIONS.md or docs/VISION.md. In tests, write such strings so the pattern does
not match the source line (e.g. build them by concatenation).

Acceptance: a ticket stopped by hard_block, approved, then retried with the same change passes the check and merges;
the same ticket with one extra matching line after approval stops again; approve on a non-hard_block page is refused;
the page shows the matched lines.

vision: a hard_block stop becomes a real user ruling: the user sees what matched and approves that exact change, and
a later change needs approval again.
removes: nothing.
